newsitem.title: UK: Gazprom reiterates its foreign holding rules.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom reiterates its foreign holding rules.

text.p: Russia's Gazprom gas monopoly reiterated on Friday that rules governing acquisitions of its shares by foreigners had not changed and warned it would take action against any breach of them.

In a letter to holders of its American Depositary Shares (ADS) released in London, Gazprom said it remained "firmly committed to its policy of a strict separation of the international and domestic markets" for it shares.

"Gazprom is working with federal authorities on measures aimed at further strengthening our ability to monitor and enforce the ringfence. Our intention is to insure that the ADS program remains the only legal and effective means by which foreign investors may acquire shares in Gazprom," it said in its letter.

It reiterated that the policy of the Russian government and its own corporate charter require that Gazprom restrict foreign ownership in the company to nine percent of voting share capital owing to the "strategic importance of the Russian gas industry to Russia's national economic and security interest.

The letter follows a heated controversy involving an international fund company which backed down from plans to invest in the domestic shares of Gazprom in the face of stiff opposition from the corporation.
Regent Gaz Investment Co Ltd had planned to take advantage of the fact that the ADSs quoted in London, cost about four times as much as Gazprom shares in Russia.

Gazprom on Friday said it was investigating several other schemes "aimed at bridging the ringfence and, in respect of these, we shall act accordingly in order to maintain the integrity of the dual- market structure".
It said it was working with the appropriate federal authorities, as described below, on measures aimed at further strengthening its ability to monitor and enforce the dual-market structure.
"Internally, Gazprom is considering making amendments...aimed at
strengthening our ability to monitor and enforce the dual-
market structure," it said.
Gazprom added that the Russian parliament is reviewing draft legislation relating to restrictions on foreign investment in strategic Russian companies but that it did not expect this
legislation will adversely affect ADS holders.
"Rather this legislation is expected to include restrictions on
foreign investment channelled through foreign-owned
Russian legal entities. Russian legislators are
scheduled to hold an important vote on this legislation
in April," Gazprom said.
The company said it would hold its annual general
shareholders meeting in Moscow and that it would issue its 1996 financial statements in July.
